findings.desc: doc-internal-contradiction: execution-plan §1 uses the phrase "mutually-distrusting vendor hosts" (line 37) — the exact framing the threat-model §3 explicitly marks as FORBIDDEN for any description of the independence claim (forbidden = "mutually-distrusting parties" / "no operator trust required"). The threat-model correctly caps the claim at cross-vendor-independent, same-operator-orchestrated, not a mutually-hostile trust boundary. The execution-plan §1 is the narrative that sets reader expectations before M1-M5; leaving the forbidden phrase there means the independence over-claim lives precisely where it shapes go/no-go decisions on M4 and M5.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 367b05322: line 38 'mutually-distrusting vendor hosts' → 'independent vendor hosts (Claude + Codex)' per threat-model §3 forbidden-wording rule.

findings.desc: doc-milestone-label-collision: execution-plan §0 (Autopilot section) uses M1/M2/M3/M4 labels to refer to autopilot-v2 milestones ("M1 (checkpoint/resume) + M2 (429/network health-aware) are production; M3/M4 (throttle, process-pool) are gated") in the same document where §2 defines M0–M5 as the Tier-C quorum milestones. A reader scanning the document cannot distinguish autopilot-M1 from quorum-M1 without re-reading from context. The collision is especially confusing at M4 where §0 says "needed only for the powered run (M4 below)" — a reader naturally reads that as a self-reference to quorum-M4 (the powered run) but it is actually pointing at an entirely different autopilot-M4. The §0 autopilot labels should be namespaced or referenced by capability name rather than sharing the M-numbering.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 367b05322: autopilot milestones renamed by capability, removing M1-M4 labels that collided with Tier-C M0-M5.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:0 evidence note is a generic template that does not address the specific verification challenge: the intent mandates grep for the exact phrase mutually-distrusting parties returns zero matches, but the phrase appears once in tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md (line 37) in a meta-context naming it as forbidden wording for M5. The evidence note (Documentation deliverable verified by review: the committed doc satisfies this intent as part of its acceptance criteria) does not document how the reviewer resolved the literal-grep vs contextual-meta-use tension. All 29 evidence notes share this same generic template. For most intents the generic note is acceptable, but for this adversarial intent with an explicit grep=0 verification criterion, the note should state: the phrase appears only within the forbidden-phrases list (a meta-use, not an assertion), not as a claim about the system.
